units.title: Society and History
units.blurb: Tocqueville on American democracy, and Marx and Engels on capital.

units.title: Science
units.blurb: Faraday's electricity, Darwin's evolution and William James's psychology.

units.title: Novels and Plays
units.blurb: Goethe, Austen, Balzac, Melville, Dickens, Tolstoy, George Eliot, Ibsen, Dostoevsky and Twain.

topics.title: Hegel: The Philosophy of Right
topics.short: Freedom made real in law, morality, the family, civil society and the state.

topics.title: Hegel: The Philosophy of History
topics.short: World history read as the story of freedom coming to know itself, from the ancient East to modern Europe.

topics.title: Mill: On Liberty
topics.short: The harm principle: society may limit what you do only to keep you from harming others.

topics.title: Mill: Utilitarianism and Representative Government
topics.short: The greatest happiness of the greatest number, and how a free people can best govern itself.

topics.title: Kierkegaard: Fear and Trembling
topics.short: A meditation on Abraham and Isaac: what faith asks of a person, and why it can't be reduced to ethics.

topics.title: Nietzsche: Beyond Good and Evil
topics.short: An attack on the philosophers' certainties, asking where our ideas of good and evil came from.

topics.title: Tocqueville: Democracy in America
topics.short: A young Frenchman travels the United States and describes how equality shapes its laws, habits and hearts.

topics.title: Marx and Engels: The Communist Manifesto
topics.short: A short pamphlet that reads history as class struggle; the lesson gives its claims and its critics' replies fairly.

topics.title: Marx: Capital
topics.short: Marx's analysis of commodities, money, labor and the factory system, and how economists have answered it.

topics.title: Faraday: Experimental Researches in Electricity
topics.short: A moving magnet makes a current, lines of force fill space, and the electric motor and dynamo begin.
topics.trouble: Only a changing magnetic flux induces a current; a magnet at rest inside a coil does nothing.

topics.title: Darwin: The Origin of Species
topics.short: Living things vary, more are born than survive, and natural selection over long ages makes new species.

topics.title: Darwin: The Descent of Man
topics.short: Darwin applies evolution to human beings and adds sexual selection; the lesson also notes where later science disagreed.

topics.title: William James: The Principles of Psychology
topics.short: The stream of consciousness, habit, attention, memory and will, from the founder of American psychology.

topics.title: Goethe: Faust
topics.short: A scholar who has learned everything bargains with the devil for one moment he would wish to last.

topics.title: Jane Austen: Emma
topics.short: A clever young woman plays matchmaker in her village and keeps misreading everyone, herself most of all.

topics.title: Balzac: Cousin Bette
topics.short: A poor relation's quiet jealousy brings down a Paris family, in Balzac's study of money and envy.

topics.title: Melville: Moby-Dick
topics.short: 'Call me Ishmael': a whaling voyage, a captain's hunt for the white whale, and everything about whales.

topics.title: Dickens: Little Dorrit
topics.short: A girl born in a debtors' prison, a man back from abroad, and a London of red tape and false fortunes.

topics.title: Tolstoy: War and Peace
topics.short: Families of Russia live through Napoleon's invasion, and Tolstoy asks what really moves history.

topics.title: George Eliot: Middlemarch
topics.short: A whole English town in one novel, and a young woman who wants to do great good in a small place.

topics.title: Ibsen: The Plays
topics.short: Modern drama begins: ordinary homes where hidden lies and duties finally come to light.

topics.title: Dostoevsky: The Brothers Karamazov
topics.short: Three brothers, their father's murder, and the great arguments about God, freedom and suffering.

topics.title: Twain: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
topics.short: A boy and an escaped slave float down the Mississippi, and Huck decides for himself what is right.
